description: Stop making the scanner device a container-creation precondition. Replace the single-node `devices:` binding with a bind mount of the /dev/input directory plus a device cgroup rule for char-major-13, and move the udev SYMLINK inside that directory so its relative target resolves in the container. After this feature the container starts at boot with no scanner attached, and a scanner plugged in later is picked up by the existing reconnect loop within 30 seconds. Access remains scoped to the one scanner by file permissions on the node (GROUP=65532, MODE=0640), which is the same mechanism as before — the cgroup rule is only an allowance, not a grant.
steps:
In deploy/docker-compose.yml, DELETE these two lines entirely:
    devices:
      - /dev/pantry-scanner:/dev/pantry-scanner
This is the change that fixes the boot failure. Do not replace it with a different `devices:` entry.

In deploy/docker-compose.yml, add a second entry to the existing `volumes:` list under the pantry service so it reads:
    volumes:
      - pantry-data:/data
      - /dev/input:/dev/input:ro
Add a comment above the new entry explaining WHY it is a directory mount rather than a node mount: a directory bind mount reflects device nodes udev creates later, so the scanner can come and go without the container being recreated. Note that :ro is safe because the app opens the device O_RDONLY (internal/scanlistener/device.go line 68 uses unix.O_RDONLY) and EVIOCGRAB is attempted but non-fatal (line 75-78).

In deploy/docker-compose.yml, add a `device_cgroup_rules:` key to the pantry service, as a sibling of `volumes:` and `group_add:`:
    device_cgroup_rules:
      - 'c 13:* r'
Add a comment stating that char major 13 is the Linux input class, that this is a cgroup allowance rather than a grant, and that which nodes the container can actually open is still decided by each node's owner/group/mode.

In deploy/docker-compose.yml, change the SCANNER_DEVICE environment value from the hardcoded `/dev/pantry-scanner` to `${SCANNER_DEVICE:-/dev/input/pantry-scanner}`. Two reasons: the new symlink lives under /dev/input, and making it overridable lets an operator point straight at /dev/input/eventN to bypass udev entirely when isolating a problem. Leave ADDR and DB_PATH pinned as they are.

Leave `restart: unless-stopped` and the `group_add:` block exactly as they are. `group_add` is what puts the container process in GID 65532 so it can read the 0640 node. Confirm both are unchanged in the final diff.

In deploy/udev/99-pantry-scanner.rules, change the SYMLINK target in BOTH commented example rules from SYMLINK+="pantry-scanner" to SYMLINK+="input/pantry-scanner". Keep GROUP="65532" and MODE="0640". Do NOT add TAG+="systemd", ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}, or ENV{SYSTEMD_ALIAS} — Design B needs no systemd integration.

In deploy/udev/99-pantry-scanner.rules, rewrite the header comment so it stays truthful under the new model. It must now say: (1) the symlink is created at /dev/input/pantry-scanner, not /dev/pantry-scanner; (2) the symlink must live under /dev/input because the container bind-mounts only that directory and udev writes a relative symlink, so a symlink in /dev pointing at input/eventN would not resolve inside the container; (3) access is scoped to the single scanner by the node's GROUP/MODE, which is why the container is NOT added to the `input` group — keep the existing rationale about not turning Pantry into a keylogger for every attached keyboard, but make clear the scoping now comes from file permissions rather than from the container seeing only one node.

In deploy/udev/99-pantry-scanner.rules, change the USB example to match on ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID} and ENV{ID_MODEL_ID} instead of ATTRS{idVendor} and ATTRS{idProduct}. Explain in a comment that udev's input_id builtin sets these ENV values directly on the event device, whereas ATTRS{} has to walk up the parent chain to the USB node and is order-sensitive. Keep the Bluetooth example matching on ATTRS{name} since that attribute is on the input device itself.

In deploy/.env.example, change SCANNER_DEVICE=/dev/pantry-scanner to SCANNER_DEVICE=/dev/input/pantry-scanner. Update the two surrounding comment lines that mention /dev/pantry-scanner (currently lines ~43-45 and ~49). Add one line noting the debugging escape hatch: setting this to a concrete /dev/input/eventN bypasses the udev symlink entirely, which isolates udev problems from container problems.

Update the compiled-in defaults so they agree with the deployment. Change `/dev/pantry-scanner` to `/dev/input/pantry-scanner` in exactly two production locations: cmd/server/main.go line ~190 (`listener.DevicePath = envOrDefault("SCANNER_DEVICE", "/dev/pantry-scanner")`) and internal/scanlistener/listener.go line ~65 (`DevicePath: "/dev/pantry-scanner",`). Also update the doc comment at cmd/server/main.go line ~168 which states the default device path.

Update the two test references to the old default so the suite agrees: internal/server/handler_scan_headless_test.go lines ~19 and ~59 both use "/dev/pantry-scanner". Change them to "/dev/input/pantry-scanner". These are assertions about the configured path, so updating the literal is correct — do not delete either test.

Search the whole repo for any remaining reference to the old path to make sure nothing was missed: look for `pantry-scanner` across *.go, *.yml, *.yaml, *.example, *.rules, *.md and confirm every remaining hit is either the new /dev/input/pantry-scanner form or a doc sentence that FEAT-003 will rewrite. Record the full list in findings.
Run `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `./scripts/test-coverage.sh`. All must pass. Commit with a message like `fix: tolerate absent scanner at container start`.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/docker-compose.yml bind-mounts /dev/input:/dev/input:ro and declares device_cgroup_rules with the rule 'c 13:* r', each with a comment explaining why.
deploy/docker-compose.yml sets SCANNER_DEVICE to ${SCANNER_DEVICE:-/dev/input/pantry-scanner}; ADDR and DB_PATH remain pinned; restart: unless-stopped and group_add are unchanged.
deploy/udev/99-pantry-scanner.rules uses SYMLINK+="input/pantry-scanner" in both examples and contains no TAG+="systemd", no ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}, and no ENV{SYSTEMD_ALIAS}.
The udev rules header explains the /dev/input placement requirement and states that per-device scoping now comes from file permissions.
The USB example matches ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID}/ENV{ID_MODEL_ID}; the Bluetooth example still matches ATTRS{name}.
deploy/.env.example sets SCANNER_DEVICE=/dev/input/pantry-scanner and documents the /dev/input/eventN escape hatch.
The compiled-in default is /dev/input/pantry-scanner in both cmd/server/main.go and internal/scanlistener/listener.go, and the main.go doc comment agrees.
No file under frontend/ is modified. No systemd unit file is added. No test or log statement is deleted.
verification: `grep -n 'device_cgroup_rules\|/dev/input' deploy/docker-compose.yml` shows the bind mount and the cgroup rule.
`go build ./...` exits 0; `go test ./...` exits 0; `./scripts/test-coverage.sh` prints PASS.
`ls deploy/systemd/` shows only pantry-update.service and pantry-update.timer — no pantry.service was added.
